jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, BigMesh, Traffic Engineering
jobs.description: Want to build a Service Mesh that powers Amazon at scale? Amazon Traffic Engineering delivers managed compute and networking solutions that help engineers build secure, highly available, and scalable services — all on top of AWS technologies. We drive the foundational infrastructure, tools, and best practices behind Amazon's global SOA expansion. As an SDE on the BigMesh team, you'll build centralized traffic management and networking solutions handling security, authentication, authorization, load balancing, and routing for Amazon's most critical services. Your work will directly improve availability, efficiency, and developer productivity by turning complex SOA concerns into managed abstractions that "just work." We use Golang, Rust, and Java. If you're new to any of these, our onboarding will get you up to speed. Come help make developing software at Amazon more seamless and flexible! Key job responsibilities - Own the full software development lifecycle for Service Mesh features, from design through implementation, testing, and production readiness. - Write high-quality, maintainable code in Golang, Rust, or Java that meets Amazon's engineering standards. - Collaborate with product managers, designers, and senior engineers to translate requirements into scalable technical solutions for traffic management and connectivity. - Design and build networking features (load balancing, routing, throttling, authentication) used by thousands of Amazon services. - Mentor junior engineers through code reviews, architecture discussions, and knowledge sharing. - Identify and drive process improvements that increase team efficiency and system reliability. - Participate in on-call rotation to resolve production issues and proactively mitigate operational risks. A day in the life - Ship code for high-impact Service Mesh features used across Amazon - Debug complex connectivity and dependency issues alongside partner teams - Review designs and guide Away-Team engineers on best practices - Advise stakeholders on technical trade-offs and effort estimates - Triage and resolve production issues during on-call rotation About the team You'll be joining the Big Mesh team, the team that owns services and connectivity solutions for Amazon's internal services. As part of this team, you'll be responsible for the ensuring we continue to develop better connectivity solutions for our Amazon teams and simplify/remove the hurdles the builders face as they navigate the complex networking architecture at Amazon. The team is always looking for ways to improve the engineer experience through process improvements and automation. You'll have the opportunity to contribute to these efforts and help shape the team's engineering practices. By joining this team, you'll play a critical role in delivering the core functionality that powers Amazon's internal connectivity solutions. Your contributions will have a direct impact on the shopping experience of millions of Amazon customers worldwide. - 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - Experience programming with at least one software programming language - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner. The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits . USA, WA, Seattle - 143,700.00 - 194,400.00 USD annually

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Amazon Leo GBO Engineering
jobs.description: Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity. The Amazon Leo Global Business & Customer Operations (GBCO) engineering team owns designing, implementing, and operating the planning systems that decide where Leo can be sold, how much capacity is available in each location, and at what price. Satellite capacity is finite and varies by geography, so our systems turn raw network coverage into a trustworthy, sellable inventory plan and enforce that plan at the point of sale so the network is never oversold. We sit between the teams that model what the network can do and the teams that operate it in real time, and we bring the business context that shapes those plans. We are looking for a talented software development engineer to help scale up and optimize the planning and simulation methods at the center of that work: the algorithms and systems that decide which cells to open for service, how much capacity each will deliver, and whether the live network can deliver it. As one of our valued team members, you will be obsessed with matching our standards for operational excellence with a relentless focus on delivering results. You will not do this alone. You will work closely with partner engineering teams across Amazon Leo. You will lead the system architecture of simulation tooling that spans multiple use cases and users, taking planning and simulation methods and making them faster, larger-scale, and production-ready, with the curiosity to engage with the substance of the problem rather than treat it as a black box. Beyond the planning and simulation work, you will contribute across the other systems our team owns. Our portfolio spans capacity, demand, pricing, inventory, and reservations, and from time to time you will pick up work on any of them as priorities and dependencies shift, from backend services to data pipelines. You will both operate systems that produce commitments the business plans against and build new ones as Leo scales worldwide. Key job responsibilities * Scale up and optimize the planning and simulation methods that turn satellite geometry and demand into capacity and coverage plans, improving their performance, scale, and fidelity. * Make large problems tractable through sound engineering: decomposition, precomputation, caching, and parallelism, proven out with measured results rather than intuition. * Build and operate the high-performance data and compute infrastructure (large-scale data stores, columnar query, batch fan-out) that lets planning run quickly. * Build systems that produce correct, trustworthy results, validating outputs against reference implementations and guarding the accuracy of numbers the business commits to. * Partner with the teams that model the network's capabilities and the teams that operate it in real time to move methods from demonstration toward production. * Contribute across the other planning systems our team owns, from backend services to data pipelines, as priorities and dependencies require. * Utilize AWS and other Amazon technologies to build highly available, scalable software services, and provide operational excellence including monitoring, alarming, and on-call ownership. Export Control Requirements: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. About the team Our team is the engineering group within Global Business & Customer Operations (GBCO) for Amazon Leo. We own the systems that connect satellite network capacity to what customers can actually buy: capacity planning, demand planning, pricing, inventory, reservations, and the data platform that ties them together. We started focused on capacity planning and have grown our scope alongside the business, so there is real room to shape new systems as Leo expands globally. We value ownership, operational excellence, and engineers who think across system boundaries. - 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - Experience programming with at least one software programming language - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent - Experience working effectively with science, data processing, and software engineering teams - Experience improving the performance and scale of computationally intensive systems or algorithms. - Exposure to optimization, simulation, or large-scale numerical or geospatial data processing, or an interest in developing depth in those areas. Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location.
